edges.why: The learner must already judge which of two very unequal sets has more before the meaning of 'more' can be tied to number rather than size.

shapes.closed-boundary.root_reason: The test only asks the child to see whether a drawn line has a gap, using the fence and sheep idea; no earlier skill in the map is needed to notice a gap, and naming or recognizing the shape is not required.

edges.why: Picking the named shape from a set means the child already sees which shapes are the same shape and which are different.

numeral.digit-formation.root_reason: Copying the digits 0 to 9 from a card is a motor skill that needs no number knowledge, so nothing earlier in the map is required.

counting.number-words.vocabulary.root_reason: Telling number words apart from other spoken words is learned by hearing them; it needs no counting, ordering, or quantity skill, so no earlier node in the map is required.

edges.why: The test starts from two rows matched one to one, and the child must see that matching shows the same number.
The test question asks whether one row has more now, so the child must take 'more' to mean number, not length.
Counting the pairs gives how many groups and counting the socks gives how many objects, so the child must already count a collection.
The statement asks for parts of equal length, so length must already be an attribute the child can attend to.
The parts must together fill the whole strip with no gaps or overlaps, the same idea as spanning a length.
The test checks the equal parts by laying one part along the others, which is a direct comparison of lengths.
Comparing a/b with 1 uses 1 written as b/b, so the equal-to-1 case rests on whole numbers written as fractions.
The rule follows by comparing a/b with b/b, two fractions with the same denominator, by their numerators a and b.
The statement itself compares the whole numbers a and b as greater than, equal to, or less than.
The statement extends the meaning of a fraction bar as division, a divided by b equals a/b, to a bar between two fractions.
The numerator and denominator are themselves fractions, which only makes sense if a fraction is a number.
The statement defines the quotient through a = b x c, which is a quotient seen as an unknown factor.
Recalling a divided by b rests on knowing the fluent multiplication fact b x c = a for single-digit factors.

rational-number.negative-as-decrease.root_reason: The node introduces the negative sign as the notation for a decrease; the test gives the amount of decrease directly, so it needs only the everyday idea of a quantity going down and no earlier skill in the map.
